title: Reading and Writing 0 to 10
short: Match a written number to a group of objects; 0 means none.
trouble: Children do not treat 0 as a number, or write some numerals backward.

blocks.html: You know how many are in a group. Now let’s write it! A numeral is the way we write a number.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: Each plate has a numeral under it. The empty plate shows 0.

blocks.html: Each numeral stands for a number of things. 0 means none at all.
Writing a numeral lets us remember how many without drawing every thing. 0 is a real number too: it tells us a group is empty.

blocks.title: Write how many
blocks.q: There are 7 apples on the plate. Which numeral do we write?

blocks.title: An empty plate
blocks.q: Nothing is on the plate. What number is that?

blocks.html: Thinking 0 is not a number, or writing a numeral backward. 0 answers “How many?” when there are none. To write a numeral, trace a model first and notice which way it faces.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: The second 3 is flipped, like in a mirror.

blocks.html: For grown-ups: Let your child write numerals in sand, with a finger on your back, or with chalk. Ask them to draw that many dots next to each one.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.CC.A.3: write numbers from 0 to 20 and use a written numeral for a count of 0 to 20 objects
